Kanjidon vs Anki 2026: Structured Study or Custom Cards?

Kanjidon Team · Feb 3, 2026

Anki is a general-purpose flashcard platform; Kanjidon is a prepared Japanese-learning app. That single distinction explains most of the trade-off. Anki lets you build almost any prompt and scheduling setup. Kanjidon removes that setup and supplies JLPT-oriented cards, spaced review and 16 quiz types. Neither choice automatically creates stronger memories, the quality of prompts and the work you do outside reviews still matter.

Quick Comparison

AreaKanjidonAnki
Product typePurpose-built Japanese mobile appGeneral-purpose flashcard system
Content6,000+ kanji and vocabulary cards in a prepared libraryYou create, import or download decks; quality varies
OrganisationKana and JLPT-oriented pathsTags, decks, fields and templates you design
SchedulingBuilt-in spaced reviewFSRS or legacy SM-2 with detailed options
Exercise variety16 quiz types, including input beyond front/back recallCard templates can be highly customised; interaction depends on the card
OfflineSelected cached flows; feature coverage variesCore local reviews work offline; sync requires a connection
CostFree path plus optional PremiumDesktop and AnkiWeb are free; official iOS app is paid; Android client is separate
Best fitLearners who want prepared Japanese content and game systemsLearners who want full control and will maintain their cards

Anki Gives You a Tool, Not a Curriculum

Anki can hold a sentence card from a novel, an audio recognition prompt, a production card or a minimal vocabulary pair. Fields, templates, tags and add-ons make it unusually flexible. The cost of that freedom is editorial responsibility: you must choose accurate content, write an answer that can be graded, and maintain the collection.

Shared decks can save time, but their sources, readings, translations and card design vary. Inspect a deck before committing to thousands of notes. A large download is not automatically a coherent course.

Kanjidon Provides the Learning Surface

Kanjidon supplies the content structure, card art, JLPT grouping and practice modes. Its library combines kanji and vocabulary cards rather than claiming 6,000 distinct kanji. The app also includes game and collection systems designed to make returning feel rewarding. This reduces setup, but it offers less authoring freedom than Anki.

Scheduling: Avoid Outdated Comparisons

It is inaccurate to describe modern Anki as “just SM-2.” Current Anki supports FSRS as an alternative to the legacy SM-2 scheduler. FSRS estimates memory stability and lets the learner select desired retention, while the legacy system remains available. Kanjidon manages spaced reviews inside its product without asking the learner to configure a general flashcard engine.

No scheduler can rescue an ambiguous card. Whether you use FSRS, SM-2 or an app-managed system, split prompts that ask for too much and grade failures honestly.

Practice Beyond Front and Back

Anki templates can include audio, typing and custom behaviour, but the learner or deck author must build the experience. Kanjidon’s 16 quiz types are already integrated and can test recognition, listening, handwriting and speaking-related tasks where supported. This is a convenience difference, not evidence that every Kanjidon quiz is necessary for every goal.

Offline and Platform Differences

Anki stores the collection locally, so core reviews can work without a connection; AnkiWeb synchronization requires one. The official desktop apps and AnkiWeb are free, while the official AnkiMobile app for iOS is a paid product and AnkiDroid is a separate Android client. Check the official download page to avoid look-alike apps.

Kanjidon can keep selected cached study flows available offline, but availability varies by feature and previously downloaded data. Network-dependent account and social functions still require a connection.

Choose Anki If

  • You want to mine sentences from your own reading or classes.
  • You need custom fields, templates, tags or specialised media.
  • You are willing to audit decks and maintain the collection.
  • Detailed scheduling control and local offline reviews are priorities.

Choose Kanjidon If

  • You want to begin without finding or authoring a deck.
  • JLPT grouping and Japanese-specific exercises matter more than template control.
  • Collectible cards, missions and varied quizzes help you keep a routine.
  • You want a free kana and N5 path before deciding on Premium.

Using Both Without Doubling the Work

A clean combination is Kanjidon for structured kanji practice and Anki for personal sentences from books, lessons or work. Do not mirror every prepared card into both apps. Give each tool a distinct job and watch the total review queue.
